With the consent of parties, heard finally.

The appellant/claimant has filed this Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 for enhancement of the compensation amount being aggrieved with the award dated 04/09/2019 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Katni in MACC No.131/2017, by which the learned Claims Tribunal awarded a total sum of Rs.3,10,700/- (Three lakhs ten thousand seven hundred)
with 6% interest to the appellant/claimant by way of compensation for the injuries, which he has sustained in a motor vehicle accident.
2.
According to claimant i.e. appellant herein, the compensation awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is on lower side and hence, need to be enhanced.

3. Since, this appeal is for the enhancement in the compensation amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal, hence the question that arises for consideration is whether any case for enhancement in compensation awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal on facts and evidence adduced, is made out and if so to what extent?
4. It is not necessary to narrate the entire facts in detail, such as how the accident occurred, who was negligent in driving the offending vehicle, who is liable for paying compensation etc.
It is for the reason that firstly all these findings are recorded in favour of appellant/claimant by the Tribunal.

Secondly, the findings though recorded in claimant's favour are not under challenge at the instance of any of the respondents such as owner/driver or insurance company either by way of filing an appeal or cross-objection.
In this view of the matter, there is no justification to burden this order by detailing facts on all these issues.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that in a motor accident which took place on 07/01/2017 the appellant sustained multiple injuries including fracture of femur bone in his right leg and learned Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.3,10,700/- (Three lakhs ten thousand seven hundred) breakup of which is as under :

2  Rs.8,000/- Towards medical expenses  Rs.25,000/- Towards special diet, transportatio  suffering and attendant  Rs.16,500/- Towards loss of income during treat  Rs.2,11,200/- Towards future loss of income
Rs.50,000/- Towards loss of expectancy of life   permanent disability

6. Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that the Claims Tribunal has assessed the notional income of appellant/injured @ Rs.5,500/- (Five thousand five hundred) per month, which is on lower side.
Learned counsel further submits that due to motorcycle accident appellant has suffered 40% permanent disability and in this regard disability certificate (Ex.P/6) has been filed.
However, the Tribunal has wrongly assessed the permanent disability as 20% in paragraph 37 of impugned award.
It is submitted that meager amount has been awarded in the head of pain and suffering, special diet, transportation, attendant and loss of income during treatment, which should be enhanced.

7. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3 opposed the prayer by contending that Dr. P.D.
Soni (AW-1), who issued the permanent disability certificate (Ex.P/6) is not the treating doctor and treating doctor has not been examined by the appellant before the learned Tribunal, therefore, the findings recorded by learned Claims Tribunal in para No.37 of impugned award is proper.
Learned counsel further submits that the learned Tribunal has awarded sufficient amount to the appellant after appreciating the evidence placed on record.
Hence, he prays for dismissal of appeal.
8. I have heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

9. From perusal of impugned award it appears that the learned Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.2,11,200/- (Two lakhs eleven thousand two hundred) towards future loss of income assessing the income of appellant @ Rs.5,500/- (Five thousand five hundred) per month, which appears to be on lower side.
Appellant was a labourer.
The accident is of the year 2017, so the income of the appellant in the year 2017 ought to have been assessed @ Rs.6,800/- (Six thousand eight hundred) per month.
Keeping in view all the facts and circumstances of the case, the findings of the learned Tribunal regarding permanent disability of 20% relating to whole body appears to be just and proper.

However, it appears that at the time of incident appellant was aged about 38 years,
therefore, keeping in view the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma Vs. DTC, 2009 (6) SCC 121 multiplier of 15 ought to have been applied instead of 16.

Keeping in view the law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs.
Pranay Sethi & others, (2017) 16 SCC 680, 40% towards future prospects should also be added.

So, the yearly income comes to Rs.1,14,240/- (One lakh fourteen thousand two hundred forty).

As discussed above, permanent disability of appellant/claimant is Kishan Chouhan vs Deepu Kol on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92461418/
3 assessed @ 20%.
Thus, the amount towards future loss of income after applying multiplier of 15 comes to Rs.3,42,720/- (Three lakhs forty two thousand seven hundred twenty).
On other heads amount awarded by the Tribunal appears to be just and proper.

11. In view of above discussion, appellant/claimant shall be entitled for the following amount of compensation :-
 Rs.8,000/- Towards medical expenses  Rs.25,000/- Towards special diet, transport  suffering and attendant  Rs.20,400/- Towards loss of income during t  months)
 Rs.3,42,720/- Towards future loss of income  Rs.50,000/- Towards loss of expectancy of l  permanent disability ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Rs.4,46,120/- Total ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
12. Thus, appeal filed by the appellant/claimant is allowed.
The appellant/claimant will be entitled for a total sum of Rs.4,46,120/- (Four lakhs forty six thousand one hundred twenty) instead of Rs.3,10,700/- (Three lakhs ten thousand seven hundred).

Thus, there shall be enhancement to the tune of Rs.1,35,420/- (One lakh thirty five thousand four hundred twenty), which shall fetch interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till the date of actual payment.
Other terms and condition of the award shall remain intact.
13. With the aforesaid, appeal stands disposed of.
14. Records of the claims Tribunal be sent back alongwith the copy of this order for information and necessary compliance.
No order as to costs.
(AMAR NATH (KESHARWANI)) JUDGE as.
